scenes.narration: Inheritance lets one class build on another. The parent class holds what is common. The child class gets all of it for free, and can add more. Write the parent's name in brackets after the child's name. If the child has its own init, it must call super dot init, to run the parent's setup too. Otherwise the parent's attributes are never created. Think of a family recipe book. The child gets every recipe, and adds new ones.

code.source:
class Animal:
    pass

class Dog(Animal):
    pass

class Cat(Animal):
    pass

d = Dog()
print(isinstance(d, Dog))
print(isinstance(d, Animal))
print(isinstance(d, Cat))
print(issubclass(Cat, Animal))
print(Dog.__bases__[0].__name__)

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: forgot super().__init__()
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. Dog has its own init, which replaces the parent's init. So the name is never stored. Printing d dot name raises an attribute error, Dog object has no attribute name. The fix is one line. Call super dot init, with the name, at the start of the child's init.

props.error:
File "animals.py", line 10, in <module>
    print(d.name)
          ^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'Dog' object has no attribute 'name'
props.why: When a child defines its own init, it replaces the parent's. The parent's setup only runs if the child calls super().__init__().

shorts.title: What is inheritance
shorts.hook: "Inheritance means a class builds on another class."
shorts.script: Inheritance means a class builds on another class. The parent holds what is common. The child gets all of it for free. Think of a family recipe book. Children get every recipe, and then add their own. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Children inherit from parents.

shorts.title: Write a child class
shorts.hook: "To make a child class, write the parent's name in brackets after the child's name."
shorts.script: To make a child class, write the parent's name in brackets after the child's name. Class Dog, brackets, Animal. Now every dog can use every method of Animal, without a single copied line. Write shared code once, in the parent. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Write shared code once.

shorts.title: super init
shorts.hook: "If the child has its own init, call super dot init, with the arguments the parent needs."
shorts.script: If the child has its own init, call super dot init, with the arguments the parent needs. That runs the parent's setup first. Then the child adds its own attributes. Super means, my parent. It saves you repeating the parent's code. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Super means my parent.

shorts.title: The missing super
shorts.script: A classic bug. The child writes its own init, and forgets super dot init. The parent's setup never runs. Later, d dot name raises, attribute error, no attribute name. A child's init replaces the parent's. Call super, and the name appears. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Do not forget super.
